rationale: PINS that a MODULE SPECIFIER is only an edge target when it is written out. `import(`data:...${x}`)` is computed - the path is assembled at run time - and the analyzer used to publish the template's LITERAL PREFIX as the module (`data:text/javascript;charset=utf-8,:*`), an endpoint no index can join. The oracle refused to derive a row for it and that disagreement is how the row was found: 1 row of 2,926 on a 200-file draw. The control rows are the same rule from the other side: a literal dynamic import and a literal require are real dependencies and must keep publishing, so a fix that simply stopped emitting dynamic imports would fail here.
